title: Speech synthesis, narration and subtitles
summary: Generate narration, align speech cues and subtitles, and prepare the required services and audio assets.

blocks.text: Microsoft Edge neural speech is Retiam’s built-in TTS provider. TTSClient uses MsEdgeTTSProvider by default, while TTS offers a global convenience facade. Node.js synthesis runs directly; browser synthesis uses a compatible HTTP proxy endpoint and therefore depends on network availability. Applications can still inject a custom ITTSProvider.

cells: Vite synthesis plugin or a compatible endpoint
Implement initialization, voices and synthesis contracts

blocks.text: The high-level speak helper prepares synthesis, coordinates scene timing and optionally subtitles/emphasis. Speak as an Animation exposes prepareAudio for precomputation. TTSClient.speak and TTS.speak return synthesized audio and durationMs; read the helper’s contract before assuming every speak function blocks in the same way.

Choose a voice ID from the current Microsoft Edge catalog and freeze the generated audio for reproducible exports. TTSCache keeps synthesized utterances keyed by text, speed and voice. Boundary timestamps can be estimated rather than true forced alignment, so inspect subtitle synchronization with the actual utterance.

TTSAudio encodes PCM/WAV and provides duration/sample information. Streaming yields progressive chunks and is useful for interactive playback; full pre-synthesis is simpler for a fixed video timeline.

Subtitles is an Entity-based caption composite using MSDF text with optional backdrop and layout controls. Place it using its documented offset/position methods and the appropriate UI layer/camera. Captions rendered through the GPU are included in framebuffer capture; a DOM caption overlay has different capture behavior.
Keep readable line lengths and enough bottom margin. Check captions at the target video aspect ratio, not only the square default playground viewport.
One synthesized sentence drives one subtitle component.
